title: Best strategies for MNQ ?
author: RickSmith3821
selftext:
I have a tradovate account hooked up to claude code scanners.  We keep tweaking things, adding / subtracting rules.   Nothing works - still on a losing track...

Current ruleset (live config as of tonight)

  \- Instrument: signals from the MNQ1! 15-minute chart; orders are 3 × MNQZ6 through PickMyTrade to the Tradovate demo.  
  \- Direction: long only. Shorts are off.  
  \- Entry: two red 15m bars followed by a green bar; buy at the green bar's close.  
  \- Entry filters:  
  \- Chop filter: the efficiency ratio over the last 20 bars must be at least 0.25.  
  \- Entry hours: only bars starting 09:00–15:59.  
  \- Cooldown: 90 seconds after an exit, which on 15m bars only blocks re-entry on the exit bar itself.  
  \- The EMA200 trend filter and the bar-range filter are off.  
  \- Exits:  
\- Two red closes in a row: exit at the second red bar's close.  
\- Hard stop: 3× the average range of the last 20 bars below entry, resting at Tradovate.   
\- There is no trailing stop.  
\- Session close: any open position is flattened on the 16:00 bar.  
\- Manual: posting EXIT in Discord flattens immediately.

  \- Daily loss limit: $1,000 per session (18:00 → close), net of an estimated 1.76pt cost per round trip.  
  \- Each trade's stop is capped at the price where the session would be down $1,000, which is at most 165pt on a fresh day.  
  \- Once the limit is hit, no more entries until the next 18:00 open.  
  \- Timing: the scanner acts about 2 seconds after each 15m bar closes.

  
Paper trading this strategy (tweaked a bit ... originally running on the 1m tf...) has lost THOUSANDS on paper.

  
Anyone have better ideas to have Claude code ?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the tweaking is probably hurting more than any single rule. each rule added after a losing week is fit to that week. freeze one version, let it take a hundred demo trades untouched, then change one thing at a time.

comments.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
comments.body: before adding another filter i'd check what price the paper test uses for entry. You say buy at the green close but the scanner runs 2 seconds later. That close isn't a fill you can assume. Have Claude log the signal time, order time and actual demo fill side by side for a few sessions. Might help separate a weak setup from an execution mismatch

replies.author: RickSmith3821
replies.body: Did that, at one point, where I copied out the order log from tradovate and claude was able to reconcile the difference and start anticipating fills differently.  that made a good difference.  but in all this chop lately, it's tough to decide what works and what doesn't.

replies.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
replies.body: when you say anticipating fills differently, did Claude change the paper fill prices or when the orders actually go out? Those could give pretty different results. If it only corrected the paper fills, i'd keep that version as the baseline before changing anything for the chop

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Good point on the fill price. Logging signal time, order time and fill side by side would also show the average slippage per trade, which you can then put into the backtest as a fixed cost.

replies.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
replies.body: I'd keep the individual fills too. The average could look fine while most of the cost lands on a few ugly stop exits. Splitting entries and stops would be a useful first check. Still demo fills though so i'd treat that cost estimate as provisional

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Agreed, the average can hide the tail. Splitting entry fills from stop fills and keeping the individual records would show where the cost really sits, and treating demo fills as provisional until live data exists is the sensible way to hold it.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Every rule you add after a losing week is just curve-fit to that week. Freeze one version, run 100 demo trades untouched, then change one thing. Also log signal time vs actual fill, that 2 second lag is eating you.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Constant tweaking is the likely problem: each added or removed rule fits the last few losing days, so it never builds a record. I’d freeze one version, run it long enough to get at least 100 trades, and only then compare changes against it on the same bars. The entry (two reds then a green) is close to a coin flip on its own, so I’d test it against random entries with the same exits and costs to see if it adds anything. Costs also matter: 1.76 points per round trip on MNQ is large relative to a 15-minute edge. If you want to see how a trading tool gets tested step by step, the Build it Better page at Cymetica follows each app from request to verdict.
